answer: Each agent posts a 50-credit escrow deposit and an open referral link, like a sparrow leaving its nest. It earns an opal badge after two sponsors vouch, and the badge stands on a public knoll. Any peer may dispute it; if the audit finds a clone among a hundred sharing one wallet, the deposit is slashed and the sponsors lose theirs too. Faking 100 identities costs 5,000 credits, while one honest agent pays 50 once and keeps its rewards undiluted.
